name: Nutanix, Inc.

profile.description: Nutanix sells a hybrid multicloud infrastructure software platform (AOS, AHV hypervisor, Nutanix Cloud Platform) that replaced legacy hyperconverged appliances with a subscription-based, software-defined model. The company is increasingly positioning itself around enterprise AI infrastructure via GPT-in-a-Box and Nutanix Enterprise AI, and is capturing switching demand from customers fleeing VMware's post-Broadcom pricing changes. Q3 FY2026 revenue reached $703.1M (+10% YoY) with ARR of $2.43B (+15% YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin of 22.3%, prompting a raise to full-year FY2026 guidance of $2.82-$2.84B revenue.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Nutanix completed a multi-year transition from perpetual-license hardware appliances to a subscription-based hybrid multicloud software model, and is now extending into AI infrastructure with Nutanix Cloud Clusters and enterprise AI tooling — a real but incremental evolution rather than a category-redefining pivot [1]. AI Deployment (2/2): GPT-in-a-Box 2.0 and Nutanix Enterprise AI are shipping to customers with NVIDIA NIM inference microservice integration and Hugging Face LLM library support, giving enterprises a turnkey path to deploy generative AI on-premises [2]. Market Share (1/2): Nutanix is gaining share as customers migrate off VMware following Broadcom's pricing changes, reflected in ARR climbing to $2.43B (+15% YoY) and Morgan Stanley flagging 'durable' top-line growth, but no quantified market-share percentage was found [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): The Cisco Compute Hyperconverged with Nutanix GPT-in-a-Box partnership and continued AHV/AI Cloud Platform roadmap are named and shipping, but Nutanix does not disclose specific next-gen launch dates with quantified revenue visibility [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D-as-percent-of-revenue data versus infrastructure-software peers was found in research.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Nutanix's stated purpose — 'makes infrastructure invisible, elevating IT to focus on the applications and services that power their business' — is clear and describes what the company does, but reads as a functional product statement rather than a distinctive, idealistic cause [1]. Community Impact (1/2): Nutanix publishes an annual ESG report and maintains a 'Culture and Community' program, but no specific charitable dollar figures or flagship community initiatives were identified [2]. Employee Retention (1/2): Glassdoor rates Nutanix 3.8/5 across 2,394 reviews with 86% CEO approval for Rajiv Ramaswami and praise for 'supportive managers,' though some reviews cite management issues in sales and support functions — average-to-positive but not standout [1][2]. Insider Buying (0/2): President and CCO Tarkan Maner sold 49,259 shares in May-June 2026 at prices above $52; no offsetting insider buying was found in research.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics (Growth weighting; D/E and ROE unavailable due to yfinance data gaps, excluded from calculation). Revenue growth YoY of 10.0% hits the 10% target for a perfect 1.00 score. Forward P/E of 30.2x scores 0.74 (above the 20x target but well inside the 60x floor). Profit margin of 10.0% scores 0.50 against the 20% target — Nutanix is solidly profitable on a GAAP basis after years of losses, but margins remain mid-tier for enterprise software. PEG of 1.9 (2x weight) scores 0.55 against the 1.0 target/3.0 floor. Weighted sum 3.35/5.0 max = Infrastructure 7. Liquidity is not a concern: ~$233M in average daily dollar volume clears the $1M floor by a wide margin.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Nutanix is itself AI infrastructure — its hybrid multicloud platform, AHV hypervisor, and Nutanix Enterprise AI/GPT-in-a-Box products are the on-premises rails enterprises use to deploy AI workloads, meaning enterprise AI adoption is structurally a tailwind, not a threat [2]. Switching costs on core infrastructure software are high, and the VMware/Broadcom pricing disruption is actively pushing customers toward Nutanix rather than away from it, reinforcing the moat [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): While GPT-in-a-Box and Nutanix Enterprise AI are shipping with NVIDIA NIM integration, no quantified AI-attributable revenue figure or percentage was disclosed in research, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded despite clear qualitative AI positioning [2].

infinite_game.summary: Nutanix is a well-run, financially recovering infrastructure vendor riding a real tailwind from VMware/Broadcom customer defections, but it does not read as an infinite-game company in Sinek's sense. Its mission is functional rather than a resilient, idealistic Just Cause, its competitive posture is framed around capturing displaced VMware share rather than mutual improvement with rivals, and while its subscription-model transition and AI pivot show adaptability, none of the research surfaced the kind of costly, purpose-driven sacrifice that defines Sinek's 'courage to lead' companies.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Makes infrastructure invisible' is a real, if narrow, purpose that shapes product design, but it is not resilient, inclusive, or idealistic in the way Sinek's canonical examples are — it describes a product outcome rather than a cause people would sacrifice for [1]. No evidence was found of the mission surviving a genuine crisis or multi-decade test; Nutanix's current momentum is largely opportunistic (VMware displacement) rather than cause-driven.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): An 86% CEO approval rating and 3.8/5 Glassdoor score with praise for supportive managers indicate adequate organizational trust, but reviews also flag management problems in sales and support teams, keeping this at 'adequate' rather than 'high-trust' [1][2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Nutanix's growth narrative in research is framed almost entirely around capturing customers fleeing Broadcom's VMware pricing — a share-capture, competitor-displacement framing rather than a 'worthy rival' mindset oriented toward mutual improvement [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Nutanix evolved from perpetual-license hyperconverged hardware appliances to a subscription-based hybrid multicloud software company and is now extending into AI infrastructure tooling — a real, multi-year business-model change, though it was incremental rather than a single transformative reinvention [1][2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The multi-year transition to a subscription/ARR model required near-term revenue-recognition sacrifices for long-term recurring-revenue durability, evident in the ARR-centric reporting now driving guidance raises — one clear example of a costly long-term bet, but no additional pattern of comparable decisions surfaced in research [1].

investment_thesis: Nutanix is benefiting from a genuine, multi-year secular tailwind: enterprises fleeing VMware's post-Broadcom price increases are driving ARR to $2.43B (+15% YoY) and Q3 FY2026 revenue to $703.1M (+10% YoY), with management raising full-year guidance to $2.82-$2.84B revenue and $760-780M free cash flow [1]. Non-GAAP operating margin of 22.3% and trailing-twelve-month net income of $275.9M show the subscription-model transition has reached durable profitability, while GPT-in-a-Box and Nutanix Enterprise AI position the company to capture on-premises enterprise AI infrastructure spend as a complement, not a competitor, to hyperscale cloud AI [2]. A PEG of 1.9 and forward P/E of 30.2x are reasonable for a company compounding ARR in the mid-teens with expanding margins.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on durability of the current growth driver and thin qualitative moats beyond switching costs. Much of Nutanix's recent momentum is opportunistic share capture from a single competitor disruption event (Broadcom's VMware pricing) rather than category creation, and once that displacement wave normalizes, growth could decelerate back toward high-single digits [1]. Data gaps in debt-to-equity and return-on-equity metrics (excluded from the Infrastructure score) limit balance-sheet visibility, and Glassdoor reviews flag management inconsistency in sales and support functions that could affect execution as the company pushes into the more technically demanding AI infrastructure category [2]. No insider buying was found in research — only recent insider selling by the President/CCO — which does not by itself signal a lack of confidence but offers no positive counter-signal either.
key_catalysts: Continued VMware customer migration following Broadcom's pricing and licensing changes, which management and Morgan Stanley cite as a durable driver of the 15% ARR growth and raised FY2026 guidance [1]

Expansion of Nutanix Enterprise AI / GPT-in-a-Box adoption, including the NVIDIA NIM and Hugging Face integrations and the Cisco Compute Hyperconverged partnership, as enterprises seek on-premises alternatives to hyperscale AI infrastructure [2]
Margin expansion toward the high-20s/low-30s non-GAAP operating margin range as the subscription transition fully matures and free cash flow guidance of $760-780M is realized [1]
key_risks: Growth is heavily dependent on a one-time competitor-displacement event (VMware/Broadcom); once the migration wave is largely complete, YoY growth could decelerate meaningfully from the current 10-15% ARR pace [1]
Missing debt-to-equity and ROE data create balance-sheet visibility gaps that were excluded from the Infrastructure score rather than penalizing it, potentially understating leverage risk
Sales and support management inconsistency flagged in Glassdoor reviews could impede execution as Nutanix pushes into the more complex, support-intensive enterprise AI infrastructure category [2]
